correctness.rationale: The upper-half-plane Bergman kernel K=-1/[π(z−conjugate(w))²] and the real differential-functional Gram product yield exactly -[u⁴+(12b−6a²)u²+120b²]/(πu⁶). The independent Fourier–Laplace positive integral confirms signs/normalization. Every u in the open upper half-plane is attainable. With y=u², Δ=12(3a⁴−12a²b−28b²); its two roots are real nonnegative precisely for c_-a²≤b≤c_+a² after separate b=0 and a=0 analyses. Outside the cone the four roots are nonreal and simple and exactly two lie in the upper half-plane; boundary double roots are real and unattainable. The included checker verified exact algebraic identities and finite sample roots without being used as a proof of all real cases.

value.rationale: The value, first derivative, and second derivative form the first natural three-consecutive-order family after recent two-term results. The complete sharp asymmetric quadratic coefficient region connects a known zero-free slice to a zero-bearing slice, reveals cancellation when both higher derivatives are present, classifies accessible zero multiplicities across the transition, and is invariant under real rescaling. These structural boundaries provide a motivated qualitative spectral/reproducing-kernel fact, rather than a routine single example or unmotivated finite numerics.
